key_decisions: D-F as-built delta (1): resize(widthCss, heightCss = _getHeightCss()) — the pinned W-5 storm scenarios call resize(400) one-arg; the height defaults to the injected provider so the W-4 CSS clamp (48px ≤375px, Phase 4) stays the single source of height truth

D-F as-built delta (2): base gained getWindow = () => window — WF-V1.4 pins listener REMOVAL from the window (pointerup/blur/resize), which is untestable without injecting the listener map (R-I7.1 no-global-patching discipline); purely additive, I-7 default shape, same convention as raf/cancelRaf/getDom

D-F as-built delta (3) — handoff-audit catch: init performs the container-measured DPR sizing (resize(canvas.parentElement.clientWidth, getHeightCss()) at end of init). The pinned init contract says 'DPR sizing + listeners' but the pinned Phase-4 wiring only calls init(document.getElementById('waveformCanvas')) at mount — with no explicit resize and no window-resize event at mount, the backing store would stay 0×0 and the waveform would never paint. This is a contract-vs-wiring gap the per-scenario tests cannot see (every test calls resize explicitly); only the Phase-4 handoff audit surfaces it

No-op render dedupe lives in scheduleRender (compare current {peaks, draft, width, height} against last-RENDERED state) rather than in _render — this is what makes WF-V1.1's 'second setPeaks of the same object → no RAF at all' pin hold (pendingCount 0, not a skipped render)

Pointer listeners attach ONLY when callbacks.onScrubStart is provided (looked up in init, not at module load) — Phase 4 ships display-only (no callbacks, untouched keyboard.spec Tab order stays green per R-2), Phase 5 wires all three; pinned by a dedicated supporting test

Draft marker is in-canvas only (second 2 px stroke in the same render pass); the view never writes vm.offsetDraft — the DOM overlay marker is VM-owned and tracks the committed offset (WF-V1.7 pins vm.offsetDraft === null after setDraft churn)
Stroke colors are canvas literals (rgba(4,120,87,·) mirroring variables.css --color-primary) — Canvas 2D cannot resolve CSS custom properties; final visual tuning is Phase 4's CSS phase

Test-side: fake canvas exposes exactly the surface the view touches (width/height, getContext, listener map, set/releasePointerCapture, focus, getBoundingClientRect, parentElement); pointer events are fired straight at the canvas listener map so 'no listener fires' is assertable without real DOM bubbling; the resize listener measures canvas.parentElement.clientWidth (the .waveform div) rather than a made-up container id — D-H assigns no id to that element
learnings: NEW learning doc 2026-08-24-canvas-proxy-ctx-mocks-must-wrap-every-called-method.md — two latent gaps in the skill's own canvas-2d.md Proxy pattern, both hit this phase: (1) an UNWRAPPED host method called through the proxy throws bare 'Illegal invocation' (canvas methods type-check this; the trap's target[prop] fallback serves an unbound function) — beginPath was the offender; wrap EVERY method the render path calls and re-apply with the real ctx as this. (2) the proxy's get trap returns the WRAPPER FUNCTION for tracked properties — asserting canvas.ctx.moveTo reads a function, not the calls; the record must be a plain object exposed separately ({ proxy, rec })

Secondary trap in the same doc: the runner's 'mocha.run() was never reached' broken-page signal (the pinned R-11 shape) is a DISJUNCTION — it fired twice for two different causes: the missing barrel export (the pinned R-11 cause) AND the new test page missing its trailing load→mocha.run() listener. After fixing the pinned cause the signal persisted identically; a pageerror + manual-mocha.run() Playwright probe disambiguates (module link failure reports a pageerror; missing scaffolding does not)
Cumulative call-log assertions must account for full repaints: each render clears and redraws the whole scene, so totals are 300 + 301 + 300 = 901, not 900 — compute render-by-render

Strict-equality position assertions need binary-exact inputs: (90/300)·3 = 0.8999999999999999 ≠ 0.9 in float64; chose 75/300 → 0.75 (dyadic). Pinned contract values (50 % → 1.5) are dyadic and stay exact

World-review with a pre-measured cost constant in the brief (0.006 ms worst-case render) produced zero performance findings and zero action items — the fifth consecutive clean/near-clean review in this project using that pattern; the three as-built deltas were sanctioned as documented

The phase-close handoff audit (writing-plans phase-handoff) caught a real contract-vs-wiring gap (init sizing) that neither the scenario tests nor the review could see — every phase file's 'Phase close' gate is load-bearing, not ceremony
